title: Heaven cannot contain thee (1 Kings 8:27)
hook: Solomon's dedication prayer admits no house can hold God

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Temple went up in quiet. Your line was finished before anyone hears it. Did you finish something without announcing it? Today the house is done, and the king who built it says it isn't big enough. Day seven hundred sixty.

The building is finished. Cedar walls, gold, the ark carried up into the inner room. Then a cloud fills the house, and the text says the priests couldn't stand to minister because of it. Solomon stands before the altar, in front of the whole gathering of Israel, spreads his hands toward heaven, and begins to pray. It's the moment the whole project was for. All that stone, all that quiet work. And partway through the prayer, he asks a question that seems to undercut the very house he's standing in.
screen: `THE CLOUD FILLS THE HOUSE.` → `HANDS SPREAD TOWARD HEAVEN.` → `A QUESTION IN THE PRAYER.`

segments.voice: The question is in First Kings eight, verse twenty-seven. Will God really dwell on the earth? And Solomon answers it himself. In the 1917 Jewish Publication Society translation: "heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee; how much less this house that I have builded!" Heaven of heavens: heaven beyond heaven. The Hebrew word for heaven is shamayim. So the builder of the Temple says, at the dedication of the Temple, that the Temple can't hold God. Not even the sky can. Then why build it? The prayer answers in its own way. Over and over in this prayer, Solomon asks that God's eyes be open toward this house, and that when people pray toward this place, God will hear from heaven. The house isn't a container. It's more like an address: a place to turn toward. Jewish tradition kept that idea after the Temple was gone. The Talmud teaches that someone praying turns toward the land of Israel, toward Jerusalem, toward the place where the house stood. There's a balance in this. A place can matter deeply and still not hold what it points to. A kitchen where someone you loved used to cook isn't that person. But you might stand in it a little longer than you need to. Solomon builds the house and, in the same breath, refuses to shrink God to fit it.
screen: `WILL GOD DWELL ON THE EARTH?` · `HEAVEN OF HEAVENS CANNOT CONTAIN.` · `NOT A CONTAINER: AN ADDRESS.` · `TURN TOWARD THE PLACE.` · then, large: `HOW MUCH LESS THIS HOUSE THAT I HAVE BUILDED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice that no place holds God. Settle, and breathe. If you have a place that feels holy to you, a synagogue, a corner of your home, a path you walk, bring it to mind. Then let the picture widen: the room, the street, the city, the sky above it, and past the sky. Solomon's words for that are heaven and the heaven of heavens. Breathe, and let the edges go. If you pray, you can turn toward a place and still let your prayer be bigger than it. If you don't, just sit with how large the space around you is. The bell holds the time.
Shamayim. The Hebrew word for heaven, which Solomon said even the heaven of heavens could not contain. Today's word.
Your line: a place to turn toward. Today, in one ordinary place, a bus seat, a desk, a kitchen sink, remember it's a place to turn toward. Day seven hundred sixty.

howItsDone: Jews read Solomon's dedication prayer in the book of Kings, and the Talmud teaches that one who prays should turn toward the land of Israel, toward Jerusalem and the place where the Temple stood.

fork.reveal: Solomon said heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain God, how much less the house he built, and asked that prayers toward it be heard from heaven.

original.note: Hebrew: heaven, the heavens. Solomon says even the heaven of heavens cannot contain God.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Temple was where God lived.
what it means: Solomon says no place can hold God; the house is a place to turn toward.
what a scholar hears: heaven of heavens means heaven beyond heaven, and the prayer keeps asking God to hear from there.

notes: Verify JPS 1917 wording at 1 Kings 8:27 (KJV: 'the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?').

Berakhot 30a on facing the land, Jerusalem and the Temple in prayer; confirm the citation.
